adjudicated.en: Taichi: "So, cleaning, can I help you?"
adjudicated.assessment: The offer to help with the cleaning is accurate, but the topic-fronted English is fragmented and unnatural for a simple offer.

highlights.text: So, cleaning, can I help you?

adjudicated.en: Miki: "You're in nice guy mode right now."
adjudicated.assessment: The observation that he is currently in his kind mode is naturally localized.
The brief confused response is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「先輩にはセクハラモードと優しいモードの二つの機能が備わっているんですよ。えっへり」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Because you come with two settings, Senpai, Sexual Harassment Mode and Nice Guy Mode. Eheh'ryh!"
comments: Can't source anything on that, uhm, moeword? See CCC3025, Yutaka's father has two optionals installed himself. Notice the absolute lack of Mass Murderer mode. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The joke that he comes equipped with two behavioral modes and the smug final vocalization are functionally retained.

adjudicated.jp: 寄せてあげることもままならない平らな胸を張った。
adjudicated.en: She pushed out a chest that you couldn't fondle by putting your hands on it.
adjudicated.assessment: The source jokes that her chest is so flat it cannot even be pushed together and lifted for cleavage. The English replaces that visual bra-related joke with an unrelated claim that the chest cannot be fondled by hand.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She thrust out a chest so flat there was nothing to push together or lift.'

highlights.text: a chest that you couldn't fondle by putting your hands on it

adjudicated.assessment: The frustrated grunt is reasonably represented.
Her teasing recognition that he is embarrassed is substantively preserved.
The emphatic denial of embarrassment is accurate.

adjudicated.en: Miki: "But you still took that so seriously."
adjudicated.assessment: Her point that his getting worked up gives him away is functionally retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「それより掃除だ。急げ、時間がないぞ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Let's just clean instead. Hurry, we don't have time!"
adjudicated.assessment: The abrupt pivot back to cleaning and demand to hurry are naturally conveyed.
The drawn-out, compliant answer is naturally recreated.

adjudicated.jp: 自分で捨てた雑巾を拾って、汚れに向かう。
adjudicated.en: Grabbing back the rag that I had dropped earlier, I turn towards the uncleanliness.
adjudicated.assessment: Dropped earlier is contextually defensible because he discarded the rag himself. The remaining defect is the abstract, nonidiomatic turn towards the uncleanliness for heading back to the stain.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he picked up the rag and headed for the stain.

highlights.text: dropped earlier, I turn towards the uncleanliness

adjudicated.assessment: The abrupt identification of blood is exactly preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「うわああああああああああああっ！！？？」
comments: So it sounds more 'cutesy' now. Troll troll troll -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The prolonged shocked scream is functionally recreated.
The surprised query is accurately represented.
The panicked identification of blood is preserved in marked, stammered English.

adjudicated.en: I can't look straight at it.
comments: But he otherwise has no problems. This is supposed to be his 'cutesy' thing. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His inability to look directly at it is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.en: I hide my face behind the rag.
adjudicated.assessment: The action of hiding his face with the rag is accurately described.

adjudicated.jp: 「は、はやく拭き取ってぇーっ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hu-, hurry up and clean it awaaay!"
comments: Fuki-totte, that last one's Youko's thing (Remove). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The stammered, drawn-out demand to wipe it away quickly is naturally recreated.

adjudicated.jp: 「はいはい、待っててください」
adjudicated.assessment: The indulgent instruction to wait is accurately conveyed.
The brief passage of time is accurately carried into the following line.
The announcement that the cleanup is finished is naturally conveyed.
The anxious question whether it is clean now is accurately conveyed.
In context, assuring him that the cleanup is complete functionally conveys that it is safe now.

adjudicated.en: I unhide my face from behind the rag.
adjudicated.assessment: The source simply says he lowers or moves the rag away from his face. 'Unhide my face from behind' is a cumbersome negative construction rather than natural physical description.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I lowered the rag from my face.'

highlights.text: unhide my face from behind the rag

adjudicated.assessment: The meaning that he cannot handle blood is recognizable, but 'weak to blood' is a game-stat calque rather than idiomatic English for this sensitivity.

adjudicated.jp: 「そんな可愛い一面があったのですね」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "So you had an adorable side to you."
comments: This may be how she knows, see CCB0008A. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her discovery of this unexpectedly cute side of him is accurately conveyed.

comments: See CCA0004, he could be talking about her as well as the blood. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker says that his physical reaction is honestly rough or hard to bear. 'That's harsh' instead sounds like a response to the preceding teasing remark and shifts the line away from his condition.

adjudicated.jp: ちらっと見ただけで、まだ気分が悪い。
adjudicated.en: I still feel sick despite having just glimpsed at it.
comments: IOW he didn't really see if it's blood. And she wiped it away in like .3 seconds! This is ridiculous. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says even a mere glance has left him still feeling sick. 'Glimpsed at' is ungrammatical, and 'despite' weakens the causal force of the small exposure producing the reaction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'One little glance, and I still feel sick.'

highlights.text: despite having just glimpsed at it

adjudicated.assessment: The apology for being useless is exactly conveyed.

comments: Connection that mascara thing was unintentional, but I guess it works too. Notice the pattern: see blood -> feel sick -> desires abuse. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source asks her to insult him by calling him a pig. The English instead calls him a worthless pig in the narration of the request and asks for general abuse, adding the judgment and weakening the specific requested wording.
The drawn-out confusion is functionally represented.
He repeats his plea to be called a pig. 'Treat me like an oinker' substitutes treatment for naming, softens 'pig,' and uses inverted, unidiomatic syntax.
The hesitant acceptance is conveyed through a drawn-out 'then.'

adjudicated.en: Miki: "Piggy wants to pig out in the pigpen?"
comments: Lit. "Pig wants to go into the prison cell", which is written "pig-box". Using "the pigs" for cops is too out of character for Miki. This oddly connects to Misato, who's the one who has all the jail and arrest stuff around her.
adjudicated.assessment: Piggy, pig out, and pigpen replace the source’s pig/pig-box jail pun with a coherent three-part English pig routine. The jail sense is lost, but the insult and comic pig-word mechanism survive.
adjudicated.remedy: Prefer a replacement that retains both the pig insult and the jail destination.

adjudicated.assessment: The pained grunt is naturally represented.

adjudicated.jp: アレンジされた上、疑問形式なのが妙にきつかった。
adjudicated.en: That arrangement being then put in the form of a question made it oddly painful.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says her improvised variation, especially being phrased as a question, struck oddly hard. The English nominalizes the whole thought into an ungainly progressive construction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Her little improvisation—and the fact that she made it a question—hurt in a strangely specific way.'

highlights.text: That arrangement being then put in the form of a question

adjudicated.jp: 「豚箱より保健室いきませんか？」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Rather than the pigpen, would you like to go the infirmary?"
comments: Is there a law that requires calling it "health room"? No, seriously, I want to know. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The alternative suggestion of going to the infirmary is accurate, but the English omits the required preposition 'to.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Rather than the pigpen, would you like to go to the infirmary?'

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Naaah, I think I'll be alright."
adjudicated.assessment: His assurance that he thinks he will be fine is naturally conveyed.
The drawn-out sound expresses hesitation or doubt. 'Uh-huh' conventionally signals agreement, reversing her response to his reassurance.
His repeated insistence that he is fine is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「そのまま一緒にお昼寝しましょう」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Let's take a nice daytime nap while we're there."
adjudicated.assessment: The invitation to take a nap together while there is naturally conveyed.
The strained reaction is naturally represented.

adjudicated.jp: その提案は、後ろ髪を引きすぎる。
adjudicated.en: That proposal made the hair on the back of my head stand way up.
comments: This is supposed to be a Standard Perverted Protagonist thing, where they're all unflappable until they're actually put on the spot. In this sense, it's fairly straightforwards: he's only interested in the sport of it, the actual deed he's more than a little reluctant, understandably given his backstory.
adjudicated.assessment: The idiom says the proposal is far too tempting to leave behind. The English reads the body-part image literally and turns attraction or reluctance to depart into alarm or gooseflesh.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'That offer was far too tempting.'

highlights.text: made the hair on the back of my head stand way up

adjudicated.en: Miki: "There are at least two beds there."
adjudicated.assessment: She adds that there are two beds. 'At least' changes the exact count into a lower bound and introduces uncertainty absent from the source.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'There are two beds there, too.'

adjudicated.assessment: The abruptly compressed farewell functionally conveys his quick exit.

comments: Girly. Well, we've been assured she IS a girl, at least. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her mild, puzzled surprise is adequately conveyed.
